history.content: How do I install additional application server instances for an existing SAP system?

You can install one or more additional application server instances for an existing SAP system. These instances are optional and can be installed on separate hosts. They can run on the host of any instance of the existing SAP system or on a dedicated host. For a dialog instance, which is an additional application instance on top of the Central Instance, you can refer to SAP Note 680617 for more information about configuring and adding it in a heterogeneous SAP environment.

Sybase is one of the many databases that can be run with SAP NetWeaver and that is supported on the IBM Cloud®. The most common architecture deployments are standard and distributed. IBM Cloud is certified for running SAP NetWeaver application servers ABAP, Java, and SAP products based on these application server stacks.

When using an SAP NetWeaver system, you have two deployment options: 
1. Central System: This is a single-host installation, also known as a two-tier setup. 
2. Distributed System: This is a multi-host installation, often referred to as a three-tier or multitier setup. It is necessary for achieving high availability and redundancy.
IBM Cloud is certified for running SAP NetWeaver application servers that support both ABAP and Java, as well as other SAP products based on these application server stacks.

Terraform is an open-source project that allows you to define your cloud infrastructure resources and services using a high-level scripting language. Your specifications are saved in a Terraform configuration file. This approach eliminates the complexity associated with using APIs, provisioning, and managing your cloud resources. Cloud providers create plugins for Terraform that include the necessary information to connect to their services. Terraform on IBM Cloud supports predictable and consistent provisioning for IBM Cloud platform resources, classic infrastructure, and VPC infrastructure. This enables you to quickly build complex, multi-tiered cloud environments and facilitates Infrastructure as Code (IaC).

Terraform on IBM Cloud enables you to define your desired cloud infrastructure resources and services using HashiCorp Configuration Language (HCL), which is a high-level scripting language. You create a Terraform configuration file that outlines these specifications. This file generates an execution plan detailing the actions required to reach your desired resource state. You can then review, modify, or execute this plan to provision, update, or delete your IBM Cloud resources. When you adjust your configuration, Terraform on IBM Cloud identifies the changes and produces incremental execution plans for your existing resources.
Can I use this to configure schematics?

Yes, you can use Terraform on IBM Cloud to configure schematics. IBM Cloud Schematics allows you to deploy and manage resources in any IBM Cloud location or region around the world. The region where you create and manage your Schematics workspaces and actions is separate from the region where your IBM Cloud resources are actually deployed or configured.
IBM Cloud Schematics executes your jobs from the region hosting the workspace and remotely accesses services to provision resources in the target regions specified by your Terraform templates. You can automate the provisioning, updating, and deletion of your IBM Cloud Schematics workspace and actions instances using Terraform.
